rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: Employers and people in control of premises must identify and assess sources of legionella risk.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: Dutyholders must manage, prevent or control identified risks.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: Correct records must be kept and maintained.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: The control framework includes an appointed competent responsible person.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: Control should begin by considering whether the water-system design can prevent the risk.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: Water services should be designed, maintained and operated to prevent or adequately control bacterial growth.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: Cleaning and disinfection arrangements depend on the system and monitoring results.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: Stagnant or recirculated water at about 20 to 45 degrees Celsius, nutrients and aerosol generation can increase exposure risk.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: Legionella risk depends on the exact water system, temperatures, stagnation, aerosols, maintenance, monitoring and susceptibility of exposed people.

rows.source: HSE Legionella and Legionnaires' disease control
rows.verified: General water-system guidance does not establish an exact parcel-level infection probability or confirm an outbreak.
